approachQuestion.prompt:
Machine factor report

Given positive N, return its prime factors with multiplicity in nondecreasing order. Return [] for N=1.

Example 1: N=180 -> [2,2,3,3,5].
Example 2: N=13 -> [13].
Example 3: N=1 -> [].

Constraints and assumptions: 1 <= N <= 10^12. Append directly to the returned list without copying existing entries. The scalar input remains unchanged. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Try d=2,3,... on remainder r=N while d<=r/d. Repeatedly remove and append d while it divides r. Append leftover r if greater than one.
options.feedback: All smaller factors have been removed. Once d exceeds the square root of r, a composite leftover is impossible.

options.text: Use repeated removal but test every integer d through the original N, even after r becomes one.
options.feedback: The factors are correct, but the fixed full range continues testing after factorization is complete.

options.text: At each d through the square root of r, remove d at most once; finally append any r>1.
options.feedback: For N=8 this emits [2,4], leaving a composite because repeated factors were not removed.

options.text: For even N return [2,N/2], for odd N>1 return [N], and for 1 return [].
options.feedback: N=45 returns [45], which is not a prime factor list.

feedback.reason: Shrink the unfactored remainder and justify a final leftover prime.
details: Set r=N. Try d=2,3,... while d<=floor(r/d). Repeatedly append d and divide r by d while divisible. After the loop, append r if r>1.

Divide out a discovered factor repeatedly to preserve multiplicity. Stop when d exceeds r/d; a remaining r>1 is then prime. Prime inputs still require all trial divisors up to the original square-root scale.

“Try d=2,3,... on remainder r=N while d<=r/d. Repeatedly remove and append d while it divides r. Append leftover r if greater than one.”: All smaller factors have been removed. Once d exceeds the square root of r, a composite leftover is impossible.
“Use repeated removal but test every integer d through the original N, even after r becomes one.”: The factors are correct, but the fixed full range continues testing after factorization is complete.
“At each d through the square root of r, remove d at most once; finally append any r>1.”: For N=8 this emits [2,4], leaving a composite because repeated factors were not removed.
“For even N return [2,N/2], for odd N>1 return [N], and for 1 return [].”: N=45 returns [45], which is not a prime factor list.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (shrinking-trials). Let N be the original input. Output append costs constant amortized time and never copies the full list. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(sqrt(N)) time, O(log N) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Worst-case prime inputs force square-root many divisor tests with fixed helper state.
details: Prime inputs force every divisor candidate through floor(sqrt(N)), making the square-root bound tight. Successful divisions number at most logarithmically many. The returned factor list is output; d and r are the only size-independent auxiliary state.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(sqrt(N)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: prime inputs force the trials; output factors are excluded.
“O(log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This counts successful divisions but omits failed trial candidates.
“O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is a loose bound rather than the tight bound for the stopping rule.
“O(sqrt(N)) time, O(log N) auxiliary space”: Returned factors are output and the method has no recursion stack.
